assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology, from the proglucagon-derived peptide to incretin biology to long-acting agonists, produced a new class of therapy for type 2 diabetes and obesity with large, clear clinical impact and a coherent physiological story.
assessment.attribution: Drucker and Holst established the biology of GLP-1 and its actions; Mojsov's early work on the active peptide form is part of the record. Knudsen (long-acting analogue development) and other credited contributors are also strong, so a three-person limit forces a hard choice and my selection of the physiology and peptide-identity contributors is not unambiguous.
assessment.maturity: Efficacy is confirmed in large, independent trials across several drugs and indications, and the interpretation is stable. Recognition is timely given the field's transformation.
uncertainties: Priority and credit among Mojsov, Habener-era work and others is contested, and some key contributors may not appear in the credited names.
The balance between physiology and industrial drug development is unresolved.
I rely on my own recollection of the literature, not verified sources.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells directed against tumour antigens are a conceptual and clinical breakthrough, producing durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and opening a new therapeutic modality.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain and June are the central figures for CD19 CAR design with costimulatory domains and clinical translation; Rosenberg contributed foundational adoptive cell transfer and early gene-engineered T-cell trials. Credit for original CAR concepts (e.g. Eshhar) may lie outside the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Several approved products and independent confirmation exist. Long-term durability is good in B-cell disease but solid-tumour efficacy and toxicity management remain limited.
uncertainties: Whether the original chimeric-receptor concept is adequately represented by the credited names.
Scope of the discovery is mostly hematologic so far.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience a causal, cell-type-specific tool and has transformed experimental physiology of circuits; originality and breadth of impact are very high.
assessment.attribution: A compound discovery: channelrhodopsin identification and characterization (Bamberg, Nagel, Hegemann), the earlier idea and first demonstration of genetic photosensitization of neurons (Miesenböck), and the mammalian neuronal implementation (Boyden, Deisseroth). Six credited names cannot fit; I pick one from each conceptual branch and recognize this is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated and adopted for two decades; mature. Clinical translation is only beginning, but the tool value is established.
uncertainties: Allocation among six plausible contributors is unresolved and any trio omits deserving people.
The prize is for a tool rather than a disease mechanism, which committees weigh differently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like-particle HPV vaccines demonstrably prevent persistent infection, precancer and cervical cancer, with population-level effectiveness data; the benefit to public health is clear and verified.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller developed the L1 VLP technology; Frazer led related VLP work and the Gardasil-era translation. Other contributors (e.g. Zhou, deceased) and parallel groups raise some credit questions, but the three credited names provide a workable configuration.
assessment.maturity: Strong evidence from trials and national programmes showing reductions in cervical disease; mature and timely, with long-term cancer outcome data accumulating.
uncertainties: Credit among parallel VLP efforts is shared and partly disputed.
Long-term cancer reduction evidence is still maturing in some populations.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response revealed a new intracellular signalling logic from the endoplasmic reticulum to the nucleus, a fundamental mechanism with broad relevance to disease, including neurodegeneration, diabetes and cancer.
assessment.attribution: Mori and Walter identified the pathway components (Ire1, Hac1 splicing, XBP1 homologue) and mapped the mechanism in yeast and mammals; the two-person configuration is clean and well supported.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is deeply confirmed across organisms for more than two decades; therapeutic translation (e.g. ISRIB-type modulators) is still early.
uncertainties: Medical impact is largely indirect so far.
Others (e.g. Kaufman, Ron) are important in mammalian branches and are not in the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense correction of SMN2 splicing produced nusinersen, transforming the natural history of spinal muscular atrophy and validating splice-modulating oligonucleotides as a therapeutic class.
assessment.attribution: Krainer defined the splicing mechanism and target sequence; Bennett led the antisense chemistry and drug development. The pair covers mechanism and translation well.
assessment.maturity: Approved therapy with strong trial and real-world outcomes; recognition is plausible but the field is still young beyond SMA.
uncertainties: Additional contributors to SMN2 target identification and clinical development may deserve credit.
Therapeutic generality of the approach is not fully shown.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Adult-stem-cell-derived organoids, building on Lgr5 stem-cell identification, gave a self-organizing culture system that has become a standard platform for studying tissue biology, cancer and disease modelling.
assessment.attribution: Clevers is the clear intellectual driver, with the Lgr5 stem-cell work and organoid culture; Sato is a major co-contributor but a single-laureate or Clevers-led configuration is most defensible. I propose Clevers alone and note that other organoid pioneers (e.g. from pluripotent-stem-cell systems) are outside this candidate.
assessment.maturity: Broadly reproduced and adopted; clinical utility such as patient-derived organoid-guided therapy is still being established.
uncertainties: Overlap with other organoid and stem-cell traditions complicates a clean scope.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of cell-free fetal DNA in maternal plasma led to noninvasive prenatal testing, now widely adopted and replacing invasive procedures for aneuploidy screening, and spawned the broader liquid-biopsy field.
assessment.attribution: Lo's contribution is singular and clearly decisive for the maternal-plasma finding; attribution is clean with one laureate.
assessment.maturity: Extensively validated clinically and independently; mature and timely. Technology refinement continues.
uncertainties: The prize-level scientific novelty may be judged narrower than the clinical impact.
Contributions from later sequencing-based method developers are not in the credited names.
